references.text: God calls Abraham and promises to bless him and make his descendants great – the same promise is renewed to Isaac here.
God assures Abraham: 'Do not be afraid, Abram, I am your shield,' and promises innumerable descendants – parallel to the assurance given to Isaac.
God establishes His eternal covenant with Abraham and his descendants and promises to be their God, which forms the basis for the words 'I am the God of Abraham, your father.'
Earlier in the same chapter, God renews the promise to Abraham concerning Isaac: to bless him, be with him, and give his descendants all these lands.
God reveals Himself to Jacob and renews the covenant promise with the same words: 'I am with you' and promises numerous descendants, in line with the promise to Isaac.
God says to Jacob: 'Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there,' a direct parallel to the assurance given to Isaac.
'Do not be afraid, for I am with you' – a direct verbal parallel to God's words to Isaac in this verse.
The book of Hebrews highlights Abraham's faith and God's promises of innumerable descendants, which is the same promise renewed to Isaac.
A repeated pattern of nighttime revelation where God confirms His covenant identity ('the God of your father Abraham') to a new generation to strengthen their faith.
Both verses use the formal title 'God of Abraham' to confirm God's identity and authority during a critical transitional period.
Jacob quoted a previous divine exhortation in the same way that Isaac received comfort and promise in 26:24.
Both verses emphasize that God's presence ('with me') is directly linked to His identity as the God of Abraham and Isaac.
Uses the same formal title to confirm that God's actions are grounded in His covenant with the fathers.
Both verses describe a divine nighttime revelation where the Lord speaks directly to a leader to confirm His presence.
